html:
The Northern Sierra Miwok are a Miwok people of the Sierra Nevada foothills in central California, along the upper Mokelumne and Cosumnes rivers, in today's Amador and Calaveras counties.

They lived in villages of bark houses with a round dance house, gathered acorns and ground them in bedrock mortars, and hunted deer. Their neighbours were the Nisenan to the north, the Plains Miwok in the valley and the Central Sierra Miwok to the south.

Their land lay in the heart of the gold country. After gold was found at Coloma in 1848, the California Gold Rush filled their valleys with mining camps like Jackson and Mokelumne Hill, and disease, hunger and killings followed. Their descendants live today at rancherias such as Jackson and Ione. See also Miwok.
